name: Robert B. Luffman
bio: Robert B. Luffman is the Libertarian nominee for North Carolina's 5th congressional district. He has worked about 25 years in transportation as a truck driver, driving in all 48 contiguous states and Canada. His campaign centers on breaking away from the two-party system.

platform.point: Challenge the two-party system and reduce partisan division.
Replace political gamesmanship with practical problem-solving.
Put constituents ahead of party and amplify NC-5 voters' voices.

notes: Rechecked the campaign site (a single page with no issue sections), Wikipedia and state party pages (blocked); no statements on specific policies were found. All ten topics remain unknown.

name: Maad Abu-Ghazalah
bio: Maad Abu-Ghazalah is a retired attorney, entrepreneur and animal rescue advocate running as the Libertarian nominee in North Carolina's 7th District. He was born in the West Bank and grew up in Saudi Arabia. He was the Libertarian congressional nominee in California's 12th District in 2002.

platform.point: Would withdraw the US from all wars that are not purely defensive and pledges not to enter new ones.
Would balance the budget mainly by sharply cutting military spending and shifting services to state and local agencies over time.
Proposes replacing the income tax with a federal sales or consumption tax on merchandise.
Wants more visas and a simpler legal process; people found without papers would pay a fine, leave and could reapply legally.
Favors private options for long-term care but says society owes everyone a safety net against catastrophic medical costs.
Would end corporate and foreign welfare so lobbyists have less reason to fund politicians.

economy.evidence: Proposes swapping the income tax for a consumption tax and ending corporate welfare, while calling for a balanced budget.

welfare.evidence: Says society owes every member a catastrophic safety net but prefers private long-term care and moving services to local agencies.

security.evidence: Criticizes ICE's use of surveillance tools and says ICE must protect civil liberties; a fairly general statement.

immigration.evidence: Backs more visas and a streamlined legal process, but says people found without documents should be fined and required to leave.

foreign.evidence: Pledges to exit all non-defensive wars, avoid new ones, cut military spending sharply and end foreign welfare.

notes: Positions come from the platform sections of his campaign site (tax, wars, immigration, budget, safety net, corruption). No statements were found on abortion, guns, drugs, energy, tech, education or religion in public life.

name: Helene Neville
bio: Helene Neville is a nurse, public health professional, endurance runner and author running as an independent for North Dakota's at-large House seat. She has worked as a travel nurse in North Dakota and as a community health consultant with the federal Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry. She has not previously held elected office.

platform.point: Would raise the minimum wage and index it to inflation.
Supports taxing corporate gains and opposes the inheritance tax.
Supports term and age limits and a pause on stock trading by elected officials and their families.
Supports protecting pre-existing condition coverage, mental health parity, price transparency and antitrust enforcement against healthcare consolidation.
Backs comprehensive reform with more immigration court resources, expanded legal pathways and protection for DACA recipients.
Supports reproductive freedom and says abortion decisions belong to patients and doctors, not government.
Wants transparency, independent review and public input before data center and AI infrastructure projects are approved.
Supports free school lunches, affordable childcare and protecting Social Security.

economy.evidence: Calls for raising and indexing the minimum wage, taxing corporate gains and antitrust action in healthcare, while opposing the inheritance tax.

welfare.evidence: Supports free school lunches, affordable childcare, protecting and expanding Social Security, and opposes Medicaid coverage cuts.

liberty.evidence: On abortion, says reproductive freedom is a fundamental right and decisions should stay between patients and doctors; no stated positions on guns, drugs or speech.

immigration.evidence: Supports expanded lawful pathways, DACA protections, a humane asylum system and more resources to cut court backlogs.

energy.evidence: Says climate change is affecting North Dakota and calls for balanced energy development with innovation and resource protection; a general statement.

tech.evidence: Calls for oversight of AI and data centers, with transparency, independent review and public participation before projects proceed.

education.evidence: Supports investment in schools, higher teacher pay, expanded Pell Grants and community colleges; she does not address vouchers.

notes: Positions come from her campaign site's issues pages. Her news page links an April 2026 report calling her a Jamestown Democrat at launch; she now runs as an independent. No statements were found on security, foreign policy or religion in public life.

name: Charles Tuttle
bio: Charles Tuttle is a Minot-area political activist and repeat candidate running as an independent against Rep. Julie Fedorchak for North Dakota's at-large U.S. House seat. He ran for the same seat as an independent in 2018 and for secretary of state in 2022. He also ran for state superintendent of public instruction in 2020 and in the 2026 special election.
notes: Searched Wikipedia election articles and tried KX News and North Dakota Monitor (both blocked); no campaign site or issue statements were found. All ten topics remain unknown.

name: Daniel Hartong
bio: Daniel (Dan) Hartong is the America First Party of Nebraska's nominee for the state's 1st congressional district, announced in September 2026.
notes: Rechecked the KLIN and Nebraska Public Media announcements (the latter was offline) and Wikipedia; no background or personal statements were found. The party platform stresses limited government, less spending and debt, and opposing new wars, but that is not his own statement.

name: David Else
bio: David Else is an Overton cattle rancher and farmer and the Legal Marijuana Now Party nominee for Nebraska's 3rd congressional district. He was the Democratic nominee for the seat in 2022 and ran for it again as a Democrat in 2024.
notes: His campaign site shows only a placeholder page, his 2022 site is offline, and the Internet Archive was unavailable. No issue statements were found; all ten topics remain unknown.

name: Macey Budke
bio: Macey Budke is a lifelong Nebraskan from North Platte who was raised in a ranching family. She works as a behavioral health practice manager and has a background in healthcare administration. She first announced as an independent and is now the Nebraska Working People Party nominee for Nebraska's 3rd district.

platform.point: Would strengthen the rural health workforce, protect rural hospitals and expand behavioral and maternal care and telehealth.
Supports teacher recruitment and retention, special education funding and more career and technical education in rural schools.
Wants policies that protect family farms and ranches, promote competitive markets and expand trade.
Seeks a fair share of federal money for rural roads, bridges, broadband, water and irrigation systems.
Supports disciplined budgeting, stronger program audits and more transparency in federal spending.
Wants more immigration judges and staff, fewer bureaucratic barriers, and border enforcement that respects due process.
Backs gun rights and concealed-carry reciprocity, plus background check enforcement and narrow threat-based intervention with due process.
Opposes limits on retroactive Medicaid coverage and proposes a Rural Coverage Stability Standard with simpler enrollment.

economy.evidence: Supports disciplined budgeting, fair and competitive farm markets, and workers' freedom to bargain while respecting right-to-work; a general statement.

welfare.evidence: Opposes Nebraska's plan to limit retroactive Medicaid coverage and calls for simpler enrollment and protection from coverage gaps.

liberty.evidence: On guns, backs Second Amendment rights and carry reciprocity but supports background check enforcement and red-flag-style intervention; on LGBTQ rights, supports non-discrimination protections.

immigration.evidence: Calls for more immigration courts and judges, fewer barriers and humane, lawful border management with due process.

energy.evidence: Backs a diversified mix of oil, ethanol and new technology and opposes rigid one-size-fits-all mandates.

education.evidence: Calls for more investment in rural public schools, teachers and special education.

notes: Positions come from her Issues and Plans pages. She does not address abortion, foreign policy, tech or religion in public life; her site notes a Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate distinction.

name: Brett Lindstrom
bio: Brett Lindstrom represented Omaha's 18th District in the Nebraska Legislature from 2015 to 2023, where he chaired the Banking, Commerce and Insurance Committee. Born in Lincoln and raised in Omaha, he played football for Nebraska and worked for about two decades in wealth management. He ran in the 2012 Republican congressional primary and the 2022 Republican primary for governor, and is running for governor in 2026 on the America First Party line.

platform.point: Proposes rolling valuation averages and lowering school levy authority to 50 cents, with more state school aid.
Would value farmland more on productive income than market price.
Wants to recruit former Nebraskans and target agriculture, manufacturing, logistics, insurance, energy and defense industries.
Prioritizes protecting public power, rural broadband and grid development.
Supports building housing near existing job centers.
Cites his law ending state income tax on Social Security benefits as a top legislative achievement.
Says AI should be governed by transparency, privacy and accountability.

economy.evidence: Pairs property tax cuts and past support for ending income and inheritance taxes with more state school aid and public power protection.

liberty.evidence: Voted to end debate on the LB933 abortion trigger ban, but also to end debate on permitless carry (LB773) and medical cannabis (LB474).

tech.evidence: Says AI needs rules built on transparency, privacy and accountability; a general statement.

education.evidence: Voted twice to end debate on LB364, a tax-credit scholarship bill for private schools, and now also proposes more state school aid.

notes: Scores draw on his Nebraska Legislature votes (LB933, LB773, LB474, LB364), his 2026 policy plan and his campaign site. No statements were found on welfare, security, immigration, foreign policy, energy transition or religion in public life.
